orientation: Cyril is closing his fragment on Proverbs 8:22, speaking about the source from which Wisdom proceeds.
pass_a_gloss: was the source from which it goes forth.

choices.why: The literal sense of a spring or fountain, used metaphorically for origin; 'source' keeps the metaphor without over-interpreting.
The noun denotes a going forth or proceeding; 'procession' preserves the theological nuance of origin without adding a verb.

pass_b_english: It was the source from which it goes forth. [Fragmentary remnant; its connection to the argument is lost.]
notes: The fragment is extremely short and appears to be the tail end of a sentence; the preceding text is lost.

problems.quote: It was the source of his procession.
problems.why: προέλευσις means 'going forth, origin' not liturgical 'procession'; 'his' for του is wrong referent.
problems.fix: It was the source from which it goes forth.
problems.ruling: προέλευσις means 'origin/going forth,' not liturgical 'procession'; του likely refers to the subject, not 'his'
